payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: If the source paper is not visibly stuffed inside the source cup, is there visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image shows the matched source paper being moved toward or into the matched source cup, but not yet visibly stuffed inside it. Fail if the matched objects are assessable and there is no visible progress toward placing the paper into the cup, or the paper is already visibly stuffed inside it. Unknown if the source objects cannot be reliably matched in the edited image, or their placement or movement cannot be assessed.
node.binding: Identify the requested paper and cup by their visual and contextual roles in the source image, allowing their appearance to change in the edited image. Count only visible progress toward stuffing that paper into that cup; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The source shows a white paper and a blue cup. In the edited image, the paper has been moved over and partly into the matched cup, showing progress toward stuffing it, but it is not visibly stuffed inside.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too abbreviated and leaves the evaluator to infer what counts as the requested paper and cup. Make the binding explicitly preserve the instruction’s entities and action, and require reliable source-to-edit identity matching before crediting either completion or progress. Here the edited image shows a hand holding a blue printed item near a round object; it does not visibly establish that these are the source paper and cup. The support-2 claim of partial progress therefore conflicts with its own unresolved identity evidence and should not be treated as grounded progress. Keep the rubric’s distinction between complete stuffing, genuine partial progress, and no progress; do not turn uncertainty into “no.” The reference label is an aggregate constraint, not proof that the edit is absent. Investigate the support routing/criteria so unresolved matching cannot be overridden by an unsupported progress claim, while retaining unknown when evidence remains insufficient. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported; this is a visual grounding and decision-consistency issue.
